subject.title: [Feature]: Auto-discovery of agent configurations from external workspaces

question: Should OpenClaw add a core trusted workspace-agent discovery/import contract, or keep agent registration explicit through `agents.list` and `agents.create/update/delete`?
rationale: The request adds a new config option, filesystem scanning, agent/session routing semantics, and config-injection risk, so implementation needs maintainer product and security intent before an automated fix can choose the boundary.

options.title: Keep Explicit Registration
options.body: Continue using central config and explicit agent RPC/CLI flows, and handle project-local ergonomics through docs, scripts, or future narrow import tooling only when a concrete gap is proven.

options.title: Design Trusted Discovery
options.body: Specify trusted roots, config filename rules, precedence with `agents.list`, validation, reload behavior, and security proof before accepting a core implementation.

options.title: Defer To Plugin Or ClawHub
options.body: Ask for an external plugin or bundle-style experiment first, then extend core APIs only if that experiment proves a missing extension point.

recommendation.title: Keep Explicit Registration
recommendation.body: Continue using central config and explicit agent RPC/CLI flows, and handle project-local ergonomics through docs, scripts, or future narrow import tooling only when a concrete gap is proven.
